detail.longDescription: I am implementing a 3-layer dense neural network from scratch using NumPy for a regression problem. I am not using TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, or any neural-network library because I want to understand the mathematical implementation of forward propagation, backpropagation, and gradient descent. I am using the Medical Cost Personal Dataset , which contains 1,337 rows after removing one duplicate. The target is charges , and the original features are: age, sex, bmi, children, smoker region, charges. My current architecture is: 15 input features ↓ Dense(32) ↓ ReLU ↓ Dense(16) ↓ ReLU ↓ Dense(1) ↓ Linear output I initialize the weights using He initialization: My current learning rate is: learning_rate = 0.001 and I train for 10,000 epochs. Model 1 Original target + engineered features Test results: MAE = 2868.78 MSE = 21564447.77 RMSE = 4643.75 R² = 0.84796 Model 2 — log1p target + engineered features Because charges is strongly right-skewed, I also tried: MAE = 2549.94 MSE = 22426241.29 RMSE = 4735.64 R² = 0.84189 Model 3 — Original target without engineered features I removed: age_squared bmi_squared age_smoker bmi_smoker and trained the same type of network with the remaining 11 features. Results: MAE = 3072.98 MSE = 23883689.66 RMSE = 4887.09 R² = 0.83161 So in my current experiments, Model 1 performs best overall in terms of MSE, RMSE and R², while Model 2 has the lowest MAE. What would be the most useful next experiment or change?
